# v2.90-dev

Automatic backups have not been running since v2.70. This release fixes that.
If you rely on the scheduled backup, please check what is actually in your
backup folder before updating — and take one now from **Run Backup Now**, which
has always worked.

## Fixed

- **Automatic backups now actually run.** Saving a schedule on the Backup page
  has been reporting "the cron entry could not be installed" and suggesting you
  check `/etc/cron.allow`. That advice was a dead end: since v2.70 the
  application runs under a restricted service account that is deliberately not
  allowed to write the system's scheduling tables at all, so the entry could
  never be created and the message pointed at the wrong thing. Backups are now
  scheduled the same way updates and report exports already are — by the
  server's own scheduled jobs, which the installer sets up — and the app no
  longer tries to write a schedule it is not permitted to write.

  **What this means for you.** Between v2.70 and this release, an enabled
  backup schedule saved your settings but never took a backup. Anything you
  took with **Run Backup Now** is unaffected, and so is everything you
  downloaded manually. If your last automatic backup is older than you expect,
  that is why. After updating, the next backup runs at the scheduled time; you
  can confirm it in `/var/log/training-tracker/backups.log` and by looking for a
  new file in the backup folder.

  One case worth knowing: if this server was upgraded *from* a version before
  2.70, it may still have had a leftover entry running backups on whatever
  schedule was set back then — so backups may have been happening, just not on
  the schedule the page was showing. The update clears that leftover and the
  schedule on the page becomes the one that runs.

- **A missed backup now runs late instead of being skipped.** If the machine is
  off or busy at the scheduled time, the backup is taken at the next
  opportunity the same day rather than waiting until tomorrow.

## Changed

- **The Backup page now tells you if nothing can run your schedule.** On a
  server without scheduled jobs installed, enabling automatic backups shows a
  notice naming the one command to fix it, instead of implying a backup is
  coming. The old message appeared only when you pressed Save and gave advice
  that could not help; this one is shown whenever the page is open and is
  accurate.

## Upgrading

No database changes, and no manual step — the scheduling entry is installed by
the update itself. After updating, open **Admin → Backup & Restore** and check
that the Automatic Backups panel shows no warning.
